scenes.heading: Properties of quadrilaterals
scenes.say: Builders check a frame is a true rectangle by measuring its two diagonals. If they're equal, the corners are square. Let's see what diagonals can tell you about every special quadrilateral.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A family: children inherit their parent's traits
scenes.science: Rectangle and rhombus inherit all parallelogram properties
scenes.breaks: kites and trapeziums aren't children of the parallelogram. They're cousins with their own traits.
scenes.say: Think of a family. The parallelogram is the parent. The rectangle inherits everything and adds right angles. The rhombus inherits everything and adds equal sides. The square inherits from both. But kites and trapeziums are cousins, with their own separate traits.

scenes.heading: Rectangle vs rhombus diagonals
scenes.say: Both have diagonals that cut each other in half. In a rectangle, the diagonals are also equal, so they make four isosceles triangles. In a rhombus, the diagonals cross at ninety degrees and cut each corner angle in half.
scenes.caption: Both have diagonals that cut each other in half. In a rectangle, the diagonals are also equal, so they make four isosceles triangles. In a rhombus, the diagonals cross at 90° and cut each corner angle in half.

scenes.heading: Rectangle diagonals
notes: Diagonals are equal and cut each other in half
scenes.say: First the rectangle, then its two diagonals crossing at O. The four half-diagonals are all the same length, shown by the matching marks. So each of the four triangles is isosceles.

scenes.heading: Inside a rhombus
scenes.say: Here is rhombus P Q R S. Angle P Q R is one hundred and thirty degrees, and the diagonals cross at a right angle at O. We want angle Q P O.
scenes.caption: Rhombus PQRS: angle PQR is 130°, and the diagonals cross at a right angle at O. We want angle QPO.

scenes.heading: Inside a rhombus
scenes.question: Rhombus PQRS has ∠PQR = 130°. The diagonals meet at O. Find ∠QPO.
scenes.say: Angle P Q R is one hundred and thirty. The diagonal cuts it in half, giving sixty-five. The diagonals cross at ninety degrees. So in triangle P O Q, the last angle is one hundred and eighty, take away ninety, take away sixty-five. That's twenty-five degrees.
scenes.caption: The diagonal halves 130°, giving 65°. The diagonals cross at 90°. So in triangle POQ, the last angle is 180 − 90 − 65 = 25°.

scenes.heading: Parallelogram with algebra
scenes.question: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are (3x + 10)° and (5x − 30)°. Find the angle next to them.
scenes.say: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so three x plus ten equals five x minus thirty. That gives forty equals two x, so x is twenty, and the angle is seventy degrees. The angle next to it is co-interior, so it's one hundred and eighty minus seventy: one hundred and ten degrees.
scenes.caption: Opposite angles are equal: 3x + 10 = 5x − 30. So x = 20 and the angle is 70°. The next angle is co-interior: 180 − 70 = 110°.

scenes.heading: Proving a parallelogram
points: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel
Both pairs of opposite sides equal
Both pairs of opposite angles equal
One pair of sides equal AND parallel
scenes.say: Any one of these proves a shape is a parallelogram. But watch out for half-facts. Equal diagonals alone don't prove anything special: an isosceles trapezium has them too. And diagonals at ninety degrees could just be a kite.
scenes.caption: Any one of these proves a parallelogram. Watch out for half-facts: equal diagonals alone could be an isosceles trapezium, and diagonals at 90° could just be a kite.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Rectangles and rhombuses inherit every parallelogram property. Rectangle diagonals are equal. Rhombus diagonals cross at ninety and halve the corners. Along a trapezium's slanted side, angles add to one hundred and eighty. And all four angles add to three hundred and sixty. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Rectangles and rhombuses inherit every parallelogram property. Rectangle diagonals are equal. Rhombus diagonals cross at 90° and halve the corners. Trapezium slanted-side angles add to 180°. All four angles add to 360°. Now try the practice questions!
